expected.raw_text: model training, evaluation, inference, and deployment

parsed.degree_signal: a PhD in ML or equivalent hands-on industry work
parsed.notes:
Who You Are, What You’ll Need, and Education/Experience supply candidate qualifications; none has an optional heading. Technologies appearing only in responsibilities or company descriptions are excluded.
The highest degree named is the PhD in Who You Are, despite the later BS/MSc qualification; industry work is explicitly accepted instead.
Foundation models are kept unmapped rather than equated with LLMs. Deep learning is an alternative to foundation models, but there is no second mapped member for that group.
The ML framework examples form alternative group 1. GCP and AWS form alternative group 2 for cloud familiarity; Docker exemplifies the separately requested containerization skill.
Agentic tools are interpreted as tool calling, and debugging is provisionally mapped to Software Testing; both mappings are flagged for review.
Vision-language models are kept unmapped rather than adding the broader Computer Vision skill. No Machine Learning skill is inferred solely from infrastructure, framework, or degree terminology.
Generic design, performance, and scalability wording is not expanded into unmentioned architecture or distributed-systems requirements.
